provenance: A Sarn repair gave an old Compact siege root shortened legs and a wider stance. The shop repeated the arrangement because it suited a machine expected to hold a road.
serviceHistory: Ridgeward militias acquired named Bulwarks when larger companies sold their older machines. Their new employers rarely expected them to march far. A walker standing beside a toll barrier or grain crossing could settle an argument without spending the ammunition the Assembly could scarcely afford.

The protected cab and large arm shield now identify a familiar sort of local security. Under that rough plate, many Bulwarks carry prized Compact emitters alongside workshop weapons. Fitters record an emitter's previous owners separately from the root's repair history. A machine can have a sound local claim and still carry a gun whose provenance nobody wishes to discuss.
fieldNotes: The standard Bulwark is already a mixed refit. Its energy weapons do not need bins, while its local gun and racks offer another supply route. Holding a useful position suits the frame; changing that decision late is harder. Cooling, ammunition and recovery prospects all matter when replacing its armament.
